summary: Over a 14-day analysis period, time-in-range (70-180 mg/dL) was 86.0% with a time above range of 8.9% and time below range of 5.1%. Glycemic stability is generally strong, though recurring nocturnal and evening hypoglycemia episodes and afternoon postprandial glycemic excursions are present. Closed-loop automation relies heavily on SMB and UAM in the absence of structured manual carbohydrate logging, while GLP-1 therapy notes indicate periodic influences on gastric emptying.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM coverage is 98.7% with 3,995 valid entries over 14 days and zero duplicate records. Data quality status is good.
analysis_steps.evidence: 3995 valid CGM entries, 98.7% coverage, max gap 65 minutes, 0 duplicate entries.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Carb treatment entries are absent from the structured treatment summary.

analysis_steps.findings: Overall glycemic control is favorable at 86.0% TIR, but 5.1% time below range indicates significant hypoglycemia risk, particularly in late-night and early-morning hours.
analysis_steps.evidence: TIR 86.0%, TAR 8.9%, TBR 5.1%, CV 32.6%, glucose extremes reaching down to 42 mg/dL and up to 293 mg/dL.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Lack of explicit carb logging prevents definitive attribution of glycemic excursions to missed boluses versus unannounced snacks.

analysis_steps.findings: Overnight basal rates maintain stable fasting glucose near target, while afternoon hours show upward glucose drift peaking around local hour 16:00.
analysis_steps.evidence: Hourly local glucose averages 90-106 mg/dL overnight; afternoon averages peak near 162.8 mg/dL with 32.1% time above range.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Exact meal timing and unannounced activity records are absent.

analysis_steps.findings: The profile uses a flat ISF of 56 mg/dL/U and a 10-hour DIA. Closed-loop telemetry dynamically adjusts sensitivity and micro-boluses.
analysis_steps.evidence: Static ISF 56 mg/dL/U, DIA 10 hours, total insulin 275.95 U across 655 entries over 14 days.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Individual insulin sensitivity curves under GLP-1 co-therapy are unmeasured.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB and UAM are enabled with smb_always_enabled=true, driving micro-bolusing in the absence of explicit carbohydrate entries.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Absence of structured meal entries requires the loop to rely entirely on UAM.

analysis_steps.findings: Max IOB (25 U) and max basal (12 U/h) provide permissive safety ceilings relative to a daily total of ~20 U/day. Dynamic ISF is active at 70% with autosens disabled.
analysis_steps.evidence: autosens_enabled=false, dynamic_sensitivity_enabled=true, dynamic_isf_adjustment_factor_percent=70%, max_iob_units=25 U, max_basal_u_per_hour=12 U/h.

analysis_steps.findings: Meal bolus strategies and carb entries are not explicitly populated in the structured logs, with the system relying on reactive correction boluses and UAM.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Detailed meal composition and timing records are missing.

analysis_steps.findings: No extended carbs or explicit absorption parameters are declared. Recurring GLP-1 injection notes indicate intermittent impacts on gastric emptying rates.
analysis_steps.evidence: GLP-1 1.25mg injection notes on Aug 14, 17, and 20; extended_carb_entries=0.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Exact meal-linked absorption metrics are unavailable.

analysis_steps.findings: The system achieves strong overall TIR but exhibits nocturnal hypoglycemia risk and afternoon hyperglycemia. Maintaining current settings while beginning structured carbohydrate logging is the safest preliminary step.
analysis_steps.evidence: Combined telemetry showing 86% TIR, 5.1% TBR, absence of explicit carb entries, and active closed-loop UAM/SMB delivery.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Need explicit carbohydrate entry data to evaluate CR and postprandial dynamics accurately.

strengths: High CGM data quality and coverage (98.7% over 14 days).
Stable overnight fasting glucose maintained by existing basal and target configurations.
issues: Recurring late-night and early-morning hypoglycemia (5.1% time below range).
Afternoon glycemic drift and postprandial elevations peaking near local hour 16:00.
Absence of structured carbohydrate logging, forcing heavy reliance on UAM and reactive micro-bolusing.

recommendations.title: Begin Structured Carbohydrate Logging
recommendations.description: With zero carbohydrate entries recorded in the treatment summary, the closed-loop system must rely entirely on UAM and reactive micro-bolusing. Logging meals will allow for proper CR evaluation.

suggested_change.rationale: Enables accurate assessment of carb ratio efficacy without altering automated delivery parameters prematurely.

recommendations.title: Review Max IOB and Max Basal Ceilings
recommendations.description: Max IOB of 25 U and max basal of 12 U/h are wide relative to a total daily insulin requirement of ~20 U/day. While not causing immediate harm, reviewing these safety ceilings reduces stacking risk.

suggested_change.rationale: Telemetry shows actual peak IOB rarely exceeds 6 U; keeping current limits avoids restricting loop responsiveness while monitoring stability.

profile_recommendation.rationale: Overnight basal rates maintain stable fasting glucose near target, and existing profile settings achieve 86.0% TIR. Changing parameters without structured carbohydrate entry data risks introducing instability.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Log carbohydrate entries and monitor postprandial glycemic excursions and overnight stability for 7 days.
profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep current profile settings unchanged while initiating structured meal and carbohydrate logging to gather baseline postprandial data.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Initiate structured carbohydrate logging for all meals and snacks to enable proper CR-based bolusing, allowing the loop to utilize COB rather than relying exclusively on reactive UAM micro-boluses.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: Zero recorded carb entries force the automated loop to rely entirely on UAM and reactive correction boluses, contributing to postprandial variability and late-night stacking risks.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Monitor postprandial glucose trajectories and time-in-range for 7 days after starting consistent carbohydrate logging.

exceptions.suggestion: Utilize temporary targets or extended absorption handling during known delayed gastric emptying windows.
exceptions.rationale: GLP-1 therapy slows glucose appearance rates, which can mismatch standard rapid-acting insulin kinetics and cause late postprandial elevations.

implementation_steps: Step 1: Begin logging all carbohydrate intake consistently for 7 days to establish reliable postprandial data.
Step 2: Monitor glycemic response and verify whether automated UAM/SMB delivery adequately covers meals once carb entries are active.
Step 3: Review nocturnal hypoglycemia patterns after 1 week of consistent meal logging before considering any basal or ISF adjustments.
education: Carbohydrate logging provides the closed-loop algorithm with Carbs on Board (COB), enabling proactive insulin delivery rather than relying solely on reactive Unannounced Meal (UAM) detections.
GLP-1 receptor agonists slow gastric emptying, which can delay carbohydrate absorption and lead to postprandial glucose mismatches if insulin is delivered strictly via standard prebolus timing.
Evaluating insulin sensitivity requires isolated correction data and structured meal records to distinguish between basal drift, carb counting errors, and algorithm adjustments.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only. The user must independently verify every proposed change, make changes one at a time, and monitor glucose closely.
TuneMyBG prepares data for review only and does not provide medical advice.
Never adjust multiple dependent insulin delivery settings simultaneously.
